summary: Sittard (gemeente Sittard-Geleen) manages parking through a paid-parking regime in the centre (1.90 euro per hour as standard, 3.80 euro per hour at short-stay sites such as Tempelplein and the station squares) and municipally owned and operated garages (Odaparking, Hub Dassenplein, ABC deck), with Q-Park running the 525-space P+R Transferium at the station. A November 2024 count showed the central garages well below capacity on a Saturday (47-74 percent). The college adopted a new parking policy outline (Parkeerbeleidsplan 2025-2040, part 1) in January 2026; it plans no extra capacity in the inner city, a gradual reduction of street parking, differentiated tariffs now and possibly progressive tariffs later. Free Sunday parking in 2024 cost about 130,000 euro and was not extended, while street works until 2027 (including a Tempelplein rebuild that keeps 51 spaces) prompted calls for parking incentives that the college was studying in early 2026.

items.text: On 27 January 2026 the college adopted the Parkeerbeleidsplan 2025-2040 Part 1 (outline note), published in the municipal gazette on 10 March 2026; it replaces parking policy parts dating from 2009 and 2012. It works in two phases: phase 1 offers alternatives and differentiated tariffs, phase 2 foresees more steering, such as fewer permits and progressive tariffs (plans, not yet rules).

For the Sittard centre the outline note says it stays reachable by car but no extra parking capacity is added in the inner city, apart from new developments under the parking norms. Street parking is to be reduced gradually once alternatives such as garages and mobility hubs exist, and the core shopping area, feeder streets and hospitality cluster stay car-light.

The outline note describes the current regime: paid parking in the Sittard centre Mon-Sat 09.00-19.00, late shopping evenings until 22.00, Sunday 12.00-18.00. Normal rate is 1.90 euro per hour (garages max 10 euro per day, no daily maximum on street); exceptions are Odaparking and Steenweg 1.90 euro per hour with a 5 euro daily maximum, Tempelplein 3.80 euro per hour for the first two hours then 5.70, and Stationsplein and Stationsvoorplein 3.80 euro for the first half hour then 5.70 per hour.

The decision on private-law parking tariffs 2025, in force from 1 January 2025, sets Hub Dassenplein and the ABC deck at 1.90 euro per hour (max 10 euro per day) and Odaparking at 1.90 euro per hour (max 5 euro per day). Geleen's Marktgarage is 1 euro per hour with the first two hours free, and leaving within 15 minutes is free. I found no 2026 version of this decision.

Garage season tickets from 1 January 2025: resident subscription 120 euro per year (Groenstraat in Geleen and Odaparking); office-hours subscription 522 euro per year and 24/7 subscription 1,065 euro per year for Hub Dassenplein, Odaparking and the Steenweg lot. Hospital garage Zuyderland (in Geleen, context only) is 1.80 euro per hour, max 8.50 euro per day.

A November 2024 parking count (reported in the outline note) found Saturday 14:00 peak occupancy of 48 percent in Hub Dassenplein (285 spaces), 47 percent in Odaparking (640 spaces, 510 net of reserved), and 74 percent in the ABC deck (275 spaces). Garages were never full except Geleen's Marktgarage (99 percent); the count also found higher parking pressure around the Sittard centre, which the note ties to a waterbed effect from missing regulation.

The December 2023 Rekenkamer report found that Sittard-Geleen owns and runs almost all its public garages itself (Odaparking, Marktgarage, Zuyderland), which is unusual for a Dutch town. For 2022 it put parking income at about 6.3 million euro and costs at about 5.8 million euro, a surplus of 573,000 euro, and concluded that the town then had no explicit integrated parking policy.

The operator Q-Park lists P+R Transferium at Geerweg 4 (Sittard station) with 525 spaces, 2 disabled spaces, 12 charge points, 1.90 m height limit, licence-plate recognition, open 24/7, and a rail-traveller discount for same-day domestic train trips. The tariff table failed to load on the page read on 21 October 2026. The 2026 gazette outline note lists the same site as Q-Park NS Transferium Station Sittard, 525 spaces, without an occupancy figure.

The college's February 2025 answers to council questions say free parking on shopping Sundays in the Sittard centre (council motion of 18 April 2024) ran from 26 May to December 2024 and cost about 130,000 euro in lost revenue, and was not continued in 2025. The college also declined a free-weekday-parking pilot and rejected copying Geleen's two free hours (in force in Geleen centre since 1 January 2025), citing the different function of the two centres; about 30 shop units stood vacant in Sittard centre in early 2025.
items.source_title: College answers to Stadspartij questions on free parking on shopping Sundays

items.text: In January 2026 the college said no free or lower parking rate would apply from 1 December 2025 in Sittard. It had decided on 8 July 2025 to make parking free on every Sunday in December, and gave about 2,000 cards worth 2 euro off in Odaparking to traders for 13 December to 4 January; in Q1 2026 it would study temporary parking incentives during the works around the centre.
items.source_title: College answers to Stadspartij questions on tailor-made parking 2026

items.text: The permit issuing rules (version valid 23 December 2025 to 6 February 2026, since replaced) allow one centre permit per address with up to 3 plates, capped per location, for example 140 on the combined Walramstraat, Heinseweg and Overhovenerstraat location and 50 each at Engelenkampstraat and Coendershof. Applications above the cap go on a waiting list.

In April 2025 the college decided to keep 51 parking spaces on the Tempelplein, whereas the earlier masterplan foresaw none after the redesign; the council discussed it on 5 June 2025. The design shown on 24 June 2025 has 51 spaces including 8 disabled spaces, and a council motion asks the contractor to keep at least 35 spaces reachable during works.
items.source_title: Letter to residents, 9 April 2025, and report of Tempelplein meeting, 24 June 2025

items.text: BESIX Infra is rebuilding Wilhelminastraat, Engelenkampstraat and Tempelplein in phases until end 2027, starting 7 April 2026 in area A (Brugstraat, Wilhelminastraat, Rijksweg-Zuid). A briefing for area B (Engelenkampstraat and Tempelplein) was announced for autumn 2026; the municipality's Centrum Sittard Bereikbaar approach covers street works in the centre between 2025 and 2027.
items.source_title: Resident letter, 4 March 2026: Reconstructie Wilhelminastraat - Engelenkampstraat - Tempelplein

items.text: In February 2025 the college admitted that the municipal Odaparking in Sittard centre had defects (water ingress, broken lifts, charge points switched off for safety). Two of three lifts were being replaced with use expected from May 2025, and the question of future ownership or privatisation was kept separate from the repair.
items.source_title: College answers to D66 questions on Odaparking Sittard

items.text: Vattenfall is responsible for new public charge points in Sittard-Geleen in 2024-2028 under the provincial agreement, with a placement policy adopted by the college on 25 March 2025. A draft traffic decision for the next round was due from 28 April 2026 with a decision on 26 May 2026.
items.source_title: MetSittardGeleen: Laadpalen in Sittard-Geleen (page read 21 October 2026)

items.text: Car ownership in Sittard-Geleen rose from 1.14 cars per household in 2015 to 1.21 in 2024 (CBS data cited in the outline note), while the Sittard core has the lowest figure at 1.02.

The Sittard Centraal programme, as shown on a municipal page read on 21 October 2026, plans a renewed station area with a 2045 vision of up to 4,689 new homes, starting with Stationspark West. The 2026 parking outline note proposes low parking norms for new development, especially in the station area, and more bicycle parking there (plans).

A June 2019 council briefing shows the Sittard street and garage rate rising from 1.30 euro per hour in 2015 to 1.90 in 2019, after increases decided in November 2017 (0.40 euro) and February 2018 (0.10 euro) and abolition of free hours in garages in November 2018. Extra income of 1.7 million euro was budgeted for 2019. This is an old fact, shown for the trend only.

gaps: https://www.sittard-geleen.nl (parkeren, parkeertarieven, Centrum Sittard Bereikbaar pages): connection timed out from my machine, so no official city-website text was read.
Regional press (De Limburger, L1, 1Limburg) and Transferium or station-area news: not read; the web-search budget was exhausted before I could search them.
Current P+R Transferium tariff: Q-Park's page did not load its tariff table, and the only figures found were on a parking-listing portal (centrumparkeren.nl), which I did not use.
No 2026 private-law tariff decision (garage rates) found, only the 2025 one; the 2026 tariff table of the Verordening parkeerbelastingen was not in the file read.
Handbook parkeerbeleid (area-based measures, expected mid-2026) and any council decision on it: not found.
Council decisions (Tempelplein, 5 June 2025; motion 18 April 2024) are known only through municipal letters and reports, not the council minutes themselves.
No Transferium occupancy or utilisation figure found; the November 2024 count covered five garages and did not include it.
The mid-2020s Sittard station-area plans (Sittard Centraal) were read on a short project page only; no parking-specific station-area decision was found.
